summary: Anachrony is a dense worker-placement/resource-engine game about racing four factions to build up tech and resilience while managing a strict day/night action-order twist and optional time-travel loops that let you undo or preload actions. It rewards long-term planning and engine-building far more than reactive tactics, with a heavy rules and iconography load especially in the first few plays.
praised: Clever, tightly integrated exogenesis/time-loop mechanism that feels genuinely novel
Strong sense of progression and engine-building satisfaction
High component and production quality (in the Kickstarter/deluxe editions)
Lots of variable setup and replayability via modules
criticised: Steep learning curve and heavy rulebook/iconography overhead
Long turns and analysis paralysis, especially at higher player counts
Time-travel mechanic can feel fiddly or gimmicky to some rather than essential
Overwhelming number of small modules/expansions for newcomers to sort through

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and shared space competition, mostly parallel engine-building

scoring.why: Points come from multiple converging tracks (tech, resources, contracts, time-rift bonuses), so winning depends on efficiently layering several scoring engines rather than one dominant strategy
